tables.comment:
One person the service knows. The registry every audience that isn't
a topic's subscribers or an explicit list walks: [`send`] with
[`SendTarget::Everyone`] reaches every row here, and an unanchored
condition — one that can match a person holding none of its topics —
walks the same rows.

A person becomes known through an act, never by being named in
someone else's: the app's server setting their attributes
([`set_person_attributes`]), a push enrollment, a topic
subscription, or a category preference. [`forget_person`] removes
the row again, with everything else the service holds about them.

columns.name: first_seen
columns.comment: When the service first knew them. An upsert keeps it.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.comment:
When the service last wrote about them: an attribute, topic, or
registry change bumps it.

tables.comment: One stored event of a campaign. Append-only.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: A UUID v7: a campaign's events list in the order they happened.

columns.name: campaign
columns.comment: The campaign.

columns.name: kind
columns.comment: A [`CampaignEventKind`]'s name.

columns.name: by
columns.comment: Who did it.

columns.name: revision
columns.comment: The campaign's revision at the time.

columns.name: detail
columns.comment: More about it.

columns.name: created_at
columns.comment: When.

tables.comment: One campaign's stored row. [`SavedCampaign`] is what callers read.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: A UUID v7: campaigns list newest first by it.

columns.name: revision
columns.comment: How many times the draft was saved.

columns.name: state
columns.comment: A [`CampaignState`]'s name.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The campaign's name.

columns.name: spec
columns.comment: The draft's spec, as JSON.

columns.name: target
columns.comment: The draft's target, as JSON, once chosen.

columns.name: note
columns.comment: The draft's note.

columns.name: send_key
columns.comment: The idempotency key of the send it was launched as.

columns.name: created_by
columns.comment: Who created it.

columns.name: updated_by
columns.comment: Who last changed it.

columns.name: launched_by
columns.comment: Who launched it.

columns.name: cancelled_by
columns.comment: Who cancelled it.

columns.name: launched_at
columns.comment: When it was launched.

columns.name: cancelled_at
columns.comment: When it was cancelled.

columns.name: created_at
columns.comment: When it was created.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.comment: When it was last changed.

tables.comment:
One person's opt-out for one category. A send skips recipients who opted
out of its category, and an inbox hides rows whose category its reader
has since opted out of, so an opt-out takes hold on what is already
stored as well as on what comes after.

The table is live: setting a preference re-runs the open inbox and
badge subscriptions of the person who set it, and the preferences
query they may be watching, without any other write.

One durable inbox row: the recipient's copy of a notification a send
delivered to them. The read, dismissed, and cancelled state lives here,
shared by every device signed in as [`Notification::person`], never
per-device.

Rows the app cancelled before they were due ([`cancel`]) stay in the
table with `cancelled_at` set, so a send's history stays explainable;
they never become visible.

One row per send and person, enforced by the database: a batch of a
fanout that replays after a crash can never write a person a second
copy of the same send.

columns.name: id
columns.comment:
A UUID v7 the service assigns, so rows order by arrival and pages
have a stable cursor.

columns.name: send_key
columns.comment: The idempotency key of the send that created this row.

columns.name: person
columns.comment: The recipient, as the app's server named them.

columns.name: data
columns.comment: The send's `data`, as a JSON object; `{}` when it carried none.

columns.name: visible_at
columns.comment: When it becomes visible: a scheduled send is invisible until this.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment: When it stops being visible. `None` never expires.

columns.name: cancelled_at
columns.comment: When the app cancelled it before it was due.

columns.name: read_at
columns.comment: When the recipient read it, on any device.

columns.name: dismissed_at
columns.comment: When the recipient dismissed it, on any device.

columns.name: opened_at
columns.comment:
When the recipient first opened it — tapped its push, or one of
the push's action buttons — on any device ([`mark_opened`]). The
first open stands; a row nobody opened, and every row written
before opens were recorded, holds `None`.

columns.name: kind
columns.comment:
The row's kind: `notification`, the inbox row this has always
been, or `data` — a silent background message's durable half. A
data row never surfaces in an inbox or a badge count; it exists so
the send's deliveries, status, cancellation, and idempotency work
exactly as they do for a visible one.

columns.name: options
columns.comment:
The send's options, as the JSON it was sent as; `None` when the
send carried none. The push engine reads it per delivery, so a
badge set to the recipient's unread count resolves at push time.

tables.comment:
One attribute the app's server set for one person: the `plan` or
`country` a segment asks about, never anything a person set for
themselves, so an audience can't be forged from the client side.

At most [`MAX_ATTRIBUTES_PER_PERSON`] rows per person; keys are
`[a-z0-9_]{1,64}` and values at most
[`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LEN`] bytes, checked everywhere an attribute is
named, the condition grammar included.

One attempt's record, per notification and endpoint: the durable
delivery the push job works through, from enqueued to accepted,
rejected, or skipped. Unique per pair, so a raced or repeated send
cannot double-enroll an endpoint for a notification.

Delivery is at-least-once: a retry after an answered-but-lost attempt
can push twice, and the provider's acceptance says it took the
message, not that anyone saw it.

columns.name: notification
columns.comment: The inbox notification this delivery carries.

columns.name: send_key
columns.comment: The send that created it, for the app's status pages.

columns.name: endpoint
columns.comment:
The endpoint it goes to. The endpoint may be gone — revoked —
while this row remains, explaining what happened.

columns.name: generation
columns.comment: Credential revision this queued delivery follows.

columns.name: person
columns.comment: The recipient, denormalized from the notification.

columns.name: platform
columns.comment:
The endpoint's platform, denormalized: the row outlives its
endpoint.

columns.name: state
columns.comment: Where the delivery stands, as [`DeliveryState`]'s names.

columns.name: reason
columns.comment: Why it left the queue, as [`DeliveryReason`]'s names, when it did.

columns.name: attempts
columns.comment: How many times it has been attempted, the first try included.

columns.name: next_attempt_at
columns.comment: When the next attempt may run, while it waits or retries.

columns.name: attempted_at
columns.comment: When the last attempt ran.

columns.name: finished_at
columns.comment: When it left the queue for good: accepted, rejected, or skipped.

tables.comment:
One enrolled endpoint: the opaque record of a device or browser the
person's app pushed them to enroll. The credential is never in it.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: An opaque id the service assigns: what lists and revocations name.

columns.name: person
columns.comment: The person whose endpoint it is, from their forwarded identity.

columns.name: platform
columns.comment: Which platform's service this speaks to.

columns.name: credential
columns.comment:
The platform's credential, verbatim: secret material, left out of
the audit log and redacted in debug output.

columns.name: generation
columns.comment: Monotonic credential revision, advanced on rotation or reactivation.

columns.name: fingerprint
columns.comment:
A SHA-256 of the endpoint's platform and destination — its token,
or a Web Push subscription's endpoint URL — in hex: how the service
knows two enrollments name the same endpoint without ever searching
on the secret itself. It deliberately does not cover a Web Push
subscription's keys, so a browser that rotates them keeps its
endpoint and its owner.

columns.name: invalidated_at
columns.comment:
When the provider said this credential no longer exists: expired,
uninstalled, or unregistered. The endpoint stays as an explainable
record and takes no further deliveries.

columns.name: locale
columns.comment:
The device's preferred locale, a canonical BCP 47 tag, as it last
enrolled: what a condition's `device.locale` and `device.language`
read. `None` when it said nothing.

columns.name: time_zone
columns.comment: The device's IANA time zone name, as it last enrolled.

columns.name: app_version
columns.comment:
The app's version on the device, as it last enrolled: what a
condition's `device.app_version` reads.

columns.name: seen_at
columns.comment:
When the endpoint last told the service about itself: its
enrollment, a renewal, or a change to its details. A send that
resolves a person's language or time zone reads their most recently
seen live endpoint. `None` for an endpoint enrolled before the
column existed, which counts as seen when it was created.

columns.name: imported_at
columns.comment:
When the app's server imported this endpoint
([`import_push_endpoints`]) from the tokens it held before the app
enrolled devices itself. Cleared the first time the device's own
app enrolls the same credential for the same person, which makes
the endpoint an ordinary enrollment. `None` for every endpoint a
device enrolled.

columns.name: apns_environment
columns.comment:
The APNs environment the device's build reported when it last
enrolled, as [`ApnsEnvironment`]'s names: which of Apple's servers
this endpoint is pushed through. `None` uses the environment the
service is configured for, as every endpoint did before the column
existed. Always `None` for an endpoint that is not APNs'.

tables.comment:
One send the app's server made. Keyed by its idempotency key, so a
retried send is recognised after a restart: the same key with the same
intent answers the stored result, and the same key with a different one
is a conflict.

A send made since the service kept a history also holds a
[`history_id`](Self::history_id), which is the order [`list_sends`]
pages in, and its category, which [`categories`] reads.

columns.name: intent
columns.comment:
A SHA-256 of the send's canonical intent: category, content,
target, schedule, and expiry. Same key, same hash; anything else
is a different send that must use another key.

columns.name: delivered
columns.comment:
How many inbox rows the send created. For a send whose fanout runs
as a job, the rows written so far.

columns.name: skipped_opted_out
columns.comment:
How many recipients it skipped because they opted out of the
category.

columns.name: targeted
columns.comment:
How many people the target matched so far: every named recipient
for a recipients send, every person the fanout matched for a topic
or condition one.

columns.name: state
columns.comment:
Where the send stands, as [`SendState`]'s names. A recipients send
is complete the moment it is made; a topic or condition send fans
out until this says otherwise.

columns.name: target
columns.comment:
The stored target, for a send whose fanout runs as a job. A
recipients send needs none: its fanout happened in its own
transaction.

columns.name: spec
columns.comment: The stored spec, for the same sends, as the JSON it was sent as.

columns.name: cursor
columns.comment:
The last person the fanout delivered to: where a replayed job step
picks up after. `None` before the first batch.

columns.name: label
columns.comment:
The send's [label](SendSpec::label), when it carried one: kept
here for every kind of send, so [`send_report`] can answer it for
a recipients send too, which stores no spec.

columns.name: history_id
columns.comment:
A UUID v7 the service assigns when the send is made: the order
[`list_sends`] pages in, newest first, and its cursor. `None` for
a send made before the service kept a history, which the list
leaves out.

columns.name: category
columns.comment:
The send's category, copied from its spec so [`categories`] can
find each category's latest send through an index. `None` for a
send made before the service kept a history.

tables.comment:
One person's subscription to one topic. Topics are per person, not per
device: the inbox is per person, and every device signed in as
[`TopicSubscription::person`] receives what the person receives.

The app's server subscribes people in batches ([`subscribe_to_topic`]);
a person may subscribe themselves, to topics the operator opened for
it, with [`subscribe`]. The table is live, so an open [`my_topics`]
page follows both.

columns.name: topic
columns.comment:
The topic's name: 1 to [`MAX_TOPIC_LEN`] bytes of the characters
FCM accepts, checked everywhere a topic is named.

tables.comment:
One wake row per person: the clock event for their open subscriptions.

The inbox and badge queries read the reader's wake row and ignore its
value, which puts `wakes` in their read set; when a send's schedule
turns — it becomes visible, or it expires — the [`wake_send`] job
writes the row of everyone the send reached, and each of their open
subscriptions re-runs with a fresh `now`, so a new item appears and an
expired one leaves without any other write. A wake that changes
nothing (the send was cancelled, the row dismissed) re-runs the query
and sends nothing, because its result didn't change.

One row per person, so the table stays as big as the audience, not as
the schedule.

columns.name: person
columns.comment:
Whose inbox time changed for. The queries read this and nothing
else of the row.

columns.name: woken_at
columns.comment:
When they were last woken. The value is a record for operators,
not something a query answers from.

tables.comment: `live.changes`: one row per written row of a live table.

columns.name: seq
columns.comment: The change's place among the database's changes.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment: The Postgres transaction that wrote it, which joins it to its commit.

columns.name: version
columns.comment: SQLite: the commit's version, set just before the commit.

columns.name: table_name
columns.comment: The changed table, with its namespace: `messages` or `billing.invoices`.

columns.name: op
columns.comment: What the write did.

columns.name: key
columns.comment: The changed row's key, in key column order.

columns.name: old
columns.comment:
The row before an update or delete, without `secret` and
`live = skip` columns.

columns.name: new
columns.comment: The row after an insert or update, without those columns.

columns.name: changed
columns.comment: For an update, every column whose value changed; empty otherwise.

tables.comment:
`live.commits`: one row per committed transaction that wrote a live
table.

columns.name: version
columns.comment:
The transaction's place in the version line. Gaps are transactions
that rolled back after taking a version, which never become visible.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment:
The Postgres transaction ID, which joins the commit to its changes.
`None` on SQLite.

columns.name: committed_at
columns.comment: When the transaction committed.

columns.name: actor
columns.comment: Who made the change, when the transaction said.

columns.name: origin
columns.comment:
What made it: what the transaction said, such as an operation's
name, or `sql`.

columns.name: lsn
columns.comment:
Replication capture: where the commit's record starts in Postgres's
write-ahead log, which orders commits as the database committed them.
`None` for commits captured by triggers.

columns.name: account
columns.comment: Whose notice it is: their account's UUID.

columns.name: action
columns.comment: The button on it.

columns.name: kind
columns.comment: `info`, `success`, `warning`, or `error`.

columns.name: read_at
columns.comment: When its owner read it.

tables.comment:
One enqueued job, in the `rpc` pack's `jobs` table.

It's a live table: a client follows a job with
[`use_job`](crate::client::use_job), and the hub sends each change. Its
policies show a job to the account that enqueued it, and to whoever
`#[rpc::job(visible_to = ...)]` names, and let only the owner change it.

columns.name: key
columns.comment:
The app's idempotency key, if it gave one: enqueuing it again returns
the same job, until the job is pruned.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The job's name.

columns.name: queue
columns.comment: Its queue.

columns.name: arguments
columns.comment: The arguments, as JSON.

columns.name: owner
columns.comment:
The account that enqueued it, as a UUID, or empty when nobody signed
in did.

columns.name: viewer
columns.comment:
Another account that may read it, from `visible_to = argument`, or
empty.

columns.name: visibility
columns.comment: Who else may read it.

columns.name: serial_key
columns.comment:
The job's name and its `serialize_by` argument: at most one job with
a key runs at a time.

columns.name: attempts
columns.comment: How many times a worker has started it.

columns.name: max_attempts
columns.comment: How many starts it gets before it fails.

columns.name: priority
columns.comment: Higher runs first.

columns.name: run_at
columns.comment: Not before this instant.

columns.name: deadline_at
columns.comment: No attempt starts after this instant.

columns.name: started_at
columns.comment: When a worker last started it.

columns.name: finished_at
columns.comment: When it reached `done`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.

columns.name: locked_until
columns.comment: Until when the running worker holds it; `None` when no one does.

columns.name: result
columns.comment: What the body returned, as JSON.

columns.name: error
columns.comment: Why the last attempt failed.

columns.name: progress
columns.comment: What it last said it was doing.

columns.name: fraction
columns.comment: How far along it last said it was, from 0 to 1.

columns.name: steps
columns.comment: The results of the steps it finished, by name.

columns.name: cancel_requested
columns.comment: Someone asked it to stop.

columns.name: failure_pending
columns.comment: It failed, and its `on_failure` mutation hasn't run yet.

tables.comment:
One mutation call that ran with a request ID, and what it returned.

Each caller sees only their own receipts: the policy compares
[`owner`](Self::owner) with the [`ReceiptOwner`] the RPC adds to the
context it runs a mutation in.

columns.name: owner
columns.comment:
Who called: their [`Identity::caller`](super::Identity::caller), such
as a session ID, or [`ANONYMOUS`] for anonymous callers.

columns.name: request_id
columns.comment: The ID the call came with.

columns.name: operation
columns.comment: The operation's name.

columns.name: arguments
columns.comment:
A SHA-256 of the operation's name and arguments, in hex: a repeat
with the same request ID and other arguments is refused rather than
answered with another call's result.

columns.name: result
columns.comment: What the call returned, as JSON.
